claim: Goldstein, Li and Wang (2026-09-03): in Polymarket 2024-01-05..2024-11-05 a one-percentage-point rise in the Trump-win probability goes with 13 bp of next-day return of Trump trades (pooled), and a probability-based strategy shows an annualised Sharpe of 1.95 over April-November 2024; the authors state the statistics are in-sample and gross of transaction costs.
quote: a one-percentage-point increase in Polymarket probability is associated with 13 basis points of next-day returns of Trump trades in the pooled sample.
limitations: Single event, in-sample, gross of costs, no independent replication found; the asset set is election-sensitive ETFs and banks, not individual stocks around announcements.
independent_replication: No independent replication found in the 2026-10-04 search.
impact_on_spec: The claim under out-of-sample test: same mechanism, same transformation, same assets and directions, a different election and period.

claim: Goldstein, Li and Wang (2026) build the strategy signal by a 5-day EMA of the daily change in the Trump-win probability, a 60-day rolling percentile rank, and a linear map to [-1, 1]; returns are equal-weighted averages across the assets, evaluation from April 1 to the election day after a 60-session burn-in.
quote: a 5-day exponential moving average to daily changes in Trump’s winning probability, converting to 60-day rolling
limitations: Single event, in-sample, gross of costs; the text does not state the EMA convention (adjust flag) or the rank tie rule, so the frozen design fixes pandas ewm(span=5, adjust=False) and average-rank percentiles.
impact_on_spec: Defines the frozen transformation of hypotheses.md.

claim: Internet Appendix Table A.1 of the Goldstein-Li-Wang paper (included in the snapshot after the main text) gives the asset directions: all ten stock ETFs, the six banks, UUP and the three connected stocks are long a higher Trump probability, the seven Treasury ETFs are short; this matches the fallback directions frozen in hypotheses.md.
quote: Up arrows indicate “long” assets expected to benefit from Trump’s policy platform;
limitations: Directions come from media coverage during the 2024 cycle; the midterm control markets measure Republican Congress control, not a Trump win, so the mapping is an assumption of the out-of-sample test.
impact_on_spec: Directions used verbatim; the frozen fallback was not needed.

claim: SECONDARY (news article, WebFetch extraction): Citigroup argues that a Democratic Congress facing a Republican president means gridlock that bond markets like, tying Polymarket midterm control odds to Treasury yields; same sign as the frozen direction of bonds short a higher Republican probability.
quote: Gridlock means fewer chances of passing large stimulus packages or tax cuts that could widen deficits and put upward pressure on yields.
limitations: Second-hand extraction of a news article on a Citigroup note; no data or test, and the note concerns Treasury yields only, not the other asset classes.
impact_on_spec: Supports the economic sign of the bond leg only; no number enters the design.

claim: Polymarket Gamma lists the events Which party will win the House in 2026 (id 32225) and Senate (id 32224), both created 2025-07-11 and ending 2026-11-04, each with separate Democratic and Republican Yes/No markets and CLOB token ids; both are unresolved on 2026-10-04.
quote: Will the Republican Party control the House after the 2026 Midterm elections?
limitations: Public API without key; markets can be edited; prices are a research input only.
impact_on_spec: Defines the signal markets and the Republican Yes tokens.

claim: Kalshi lists CONTROLH-2026 and CONTROLS-2026 with Democratic and Republican markets open since 2024-11-06 (public candlestick endpoint, no key); used only as the robustness signal.
quote: Which party will win the U.S. House?
limitations: Public market data only; no account, order or key.

claim: The public CLOB /prices-history endpoint returns timestamped prices for a resolved market (daily points for fidelity 1440 in the probe); the intel notes record that hourly and finer history needs startTs/endTs windows and that interval=max with fidelity 60 returned empty.
limitations: Probe covered one market; whether every earnings token has hourly history is the first coverage question of the build and is reported in data-feasibility.json; thin markets can have no print for days (stale flag).
impact_on_spec: Data source for the daily 4 pm probabilities of the control markets.

claim: Kalshi distributions are accurate forecasts of macro outcomes (for headline CPI a statistically significant improvement over the Bloomberg consensus); the paper tests forecast accuracy and news response, not stock returns.
quote: for headline CPI, we find Kalshi provides a statistically significant improvement over the Bloomberg consensus forecast.
limitations: Macro releases on Kalshi, not company earnings on Polymarket; accuracy is not the same as tradable alpha after the stock market already prices the information.
independent_replication: Replication code by a third party (WillBtK/macro_kalshi) rebuilds the distributions; no independent replication of the forecast claims found.
impact_on_spec: Shows regulated event-contract prices carry real information; motivates the Kalshi robustness signal, no stock-return test.

claim: Qin and Yang (arXiv 2606.04217) describe the Polymarket-v1 on-chain trade archive, 2022-11-21 to 2026-04-28, 1.20 billion trades, and show that tick-rule and bulk-volume classifiers are near random on it.
quote: We introduce the Polymarket-v1 Database: the complete on-chain trade archive
limitations: A data and microstructure paper with no stock-return test.
impact_on_spec: Last prints in thin Polymarket markets are noisy; the daily 16:00 ET price is taken from the last CLOB point and a missing session carries the last price.

claim: Leigh, Wolfers and Zitzewitz (NBER w9587, 2003): the price of a prediction-market security on Saddam Hussein's survival moves with spot oil and equity-sector prices, so an event probability can be mapped to asset returns by a stated policy channel; 20-year-old precedent for translating event odds into asset exposures.
quote: The spot oil price has moved closely with the Saddam Security,
limitations: Different event, a 2003 high-frequency study of one security, no trading strategy or costs; the intel snapshot was read from the NBER PDF text.
impact_on_spec: Precedent for the mapping of event odds to policy-sensitive assets; no number enters the design.
